blocks.text: Early complex societies in the Americas show that civilization did not require a reproduction of Eurasian conditions. Different animals, crops, terrain and transport arrangements still supported large settlements, public buildings, exchange and political life. The absence of a familiar technology is not the absence of complexity.

Andean coasts, highlands and valleys offered different resources. Connecting ecological zones supported arrangements unlike those based on broad agricultural plains. Mesoamerica had its own accumulations and rhythms, so the Americas cannot be assigned a single civilizational timetable.

blocks.caption: Nubian Kush Formation · Context illustration; historical interpretation is in the text.

blocks.text: African complexity likewise cannot be sought only along the Nile and Mediterranean. Regional farming, pastoralism, exchange and political organization must be understood through local conditions and external connections. Making one region the standard hides other paths.

Early urban societies shared problems of coordinating people, resources and memory, but could answer them differently. Common capabilities did not entail identical institutions. Civilizational divergence unfolded as those different conditions and choices accumulated.
